tier_rationale: The manufacturer's own owner's guide lists exactly three controls — a power switch, a 3-position heat selector, and a mechanical thermostat dial — with no mention anywhere in the 13-page manual of wifi, an app, Bluetooth, or a remote. Vornado Air LLC (FCC grantee code WOT) holds FCC grants for other heater models with RF remotes (e.g. WOTTVH600, described as 'Fan Heater (315MHz Tx)'), so the vendor demonstrably files when a heater has a radio, and no grant of any kind exists for the VH200.
the_unplug_test: Nothing changes; the VH200 was never on your network. You plug it into a wall outlet, flip the power switch, pick a wattage (750/1125/1500W), and turn the mechanical thermostat dial until the room feels right — the dial's internal bimetal contact cycles the heating element on and off to hold that temperature. There is no app, no account, and no firmware, so there is nothing for a router being off to affect.

repairability.notes: Manual states the unit has no user-serviceable parts and that opening the case voids the warranty; Vornado's stated repair path is to return the unit to the factory. Sealed, permanently-lubricated motor.

sources.supports: Official Vornado owner's guide for model VH200. Controls section (p.7) lists only Power On/Off, Heat (3 wattage settings), and Thermostat (mechanical dial). No mention anywhere in the manual of wifi, app, Bluetooth, or remote control; troubleshooting and safety sections describe only mechanical/electrical fault conditions (overheat cutoff, tip-over switch, breaker trips).

Sibling control: Vornado Air LLC, grantee code WOT, holds 19 FCC grants including WOTTVH600 ('RF Remote Control (315MHz Tx)') and WOTTVH600-2 ('Fan Heater (315MHz Tx)') for a different, remote-equipped heater model, plus several remote-control grants for its fan and humidifier lines. No grant of any kind exists for VH200, confirming the vendor files when a product has a radio and that the absence here is meaningful.
Manufacturer product page confirms price ($74.99), wattage settings, and describes the unit as manual-control with a thermostatic dial; no smart features listed.

notes: Vornado sells this same mechanical control layout across most of its compact heater line; the exception to watch for is any model with 'Remote' printed on the box, since the manufacturer does sell RF-remote heaters (e.g. TVH600) under a visually similar case design.
